result.summary: The image depicts a signalized urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks and continuous sidewalks. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the environment lacks physical buffers between the walkway and traffic, and parked vehicles near the corners create potential sightline obstructions.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection and crosswalk may block the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, near the blue car and the hair salon.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The image shows a residential urban environment with a continuous concrete sidewalk adjacent to brick buildings. Parallel parking is present along the curb, providing a buffer from the roadway but also creating potential visual obstructions.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicle
hazards.description: A large SUV parked at the curb obscures sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Introduce street trees to provide a more robust physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install lighting fixtures to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians during evening and night hours.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban street with continuous sidewalks on both sides and dense parallel parking. While the narrow roadway likely encourages lower vehicle speeds, the lack of marked crossings and the visual obstructions created by parked cars present risks for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street obscures pedestrians, particularly children, from the view of oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crossing points, which may lead to unpredictable mid-block crossings.

interventions.title: Daylighting

interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at intersections to shorten crossing distances and prevent parking too close to corners.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to ensure vehicle speeds remain low in this residential/mixed-use context.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with a continuous concrete sidewalk that lacks a buffer from the roadway. Significant obstructions are present in the form of utility poles placed directly in the pedestrian path, which restricts accessibility and narrows the effective walking width.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located in the center of the sidewalk, significantly narrowing the clear path for pedestrians and creating a barrier for those with mobility aids.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is immediately adjacent to the parking and travel lanes without a furniture zone or planting strip to separate pedestrians from vehicles.
